# Lane W: the static world's tables in Rust, shadow mode (2026-10-26)

Part of `docs/2026-10-26-rust-scene-core.md` (plan, contract, lanes). Design: `docs/2026-10-26-rust-residency-design.md`
(R2), steps S0 and S2 of §4.

Evidence tags: **[M]** measured (source named), **[D]** derived, **[C]** code read. Lane rule (CLAUDE.md): node tests
only, one at a time; nothing here was compiled, run in a browser or measured on the 1070. The Rust is uncompiled
until the orchestrator's `cargo test -p holtburger-scene` and wasm build.

## 1. S0: the per-group census

`scene3d/rust/world.js` `worldGroupCensus(scene3d)`, published as `globalThis.__hbWorldGroupCensus` and read by
`frame_split.js` `frameSplitCensus()` as its new `groups` field (no import: the probe's module graph is unchanged).
Structure only, frame_split's own rule: no frustum is re-derived.

- **resident**: every node under the root. **visited**: reachable without crossing `visible === false` (what
  `projectObject` and each shadow cascade walk). **composing**: visited and `matrixAutoUpdate` (composes every frame
  under `?skipHiddenMatrix`, default on). **composingAll**: resident and `matrixAutoUpdate` (composes every frame
  without it). **frozen**: `matrixAutoUpdate === false`.
- **offGraphAnchors**: the `?anchorOffGraph` per-landblock roots (`staticsGroup.userData.__anchorRoots`): never in the
  scene, counted resident only.
- `total` sums every group.

Owed on the 1070: the census at Holtburg and Linvak on the chain default (R2 §6 item 1):
`__frameSplitCensus().groups` (no flag needed; statics.js loads world.js), or `__rustWorld.groups()` when
`?rustWorld=on` armed the bridge.

## 2. S0: the recorder and the fixtures

- `tools/rust_parity/gen_world_scenarios.mjs`: six scripted worlds through the REAL producers in node, three headless:
  - `chunk` / `chunkDedup` (`static_batch_x.js`, `?statGeomDedup` off / on with stamped content keys): four
    landblocks over two 3×3-LB regions, a value-merged material pair, a 270-instance group (the bucket grows past
    its 256 first allocation), LRU park / unpark / evict / `disposeParked` / teardown, `?objRadius` hide / show /
    `afterUnpark` / `afterObjectBake` / forget, a re-bake of a PARKED hidden landblock (the late-track merge re-applies
    the park hide), the optimize tick, bucket reaping;
  - `atlas` (`static_atlas.js`): feeds incl. growth past the first instance allocation, park / unpark, `?objRadius`,
    evict + optimize, teardown;
  - `building` (`buildings.js` `consolidateBuildingSurfaces`): batches baked, parked (detached whole), unparked,
    evicted (disposed);
  - `pool` (`pool_registry.js`): stage-A feeds, a plan parked mid-feed (commit INTO the parked state), adopt, sticky
    landblock hides across commit / park / adopt, both cell-PVS forms, band swaps, a cell release that empties a
    record while its pool survives, abandon, tile release with optimize and reap, park marks on resident and
    non-resident tiles, registry dispose;
  - `grid` (`residency_grid.js` SlotGrid + GridResidencyAdapter, legacy-lane arm) wired as index.js wires it: feeds
    bake chunk buckets and pool plans and track a REAL `LandblockLRU`; slot-state events park / adopt / release the
    pools; `?objRadius` per crossing; a walk east, a stand-still (hysteresis parks 12 tiles), a teleport (drain),
    pressure releases past the 30 s floor, a teleport back (re-adopt), adapter dispose. Its `?objRadius` → pool hide
    hooks are NOT wired (unchanged since 10-26, so its fixture stays byte-identical); `objrPool` wires them;
  - `objrPool` (2026-10-29, §11): the same grid world (`gridWorld`, `?objRadius` 1) with `_poolHideLb` /
    `_poolShowLb` wired to the registry as index.js wires them: landblock A hidden for distance while resident, its
    tile parked on a teleport and released by the pressure pass, a crossing far away forgets it, a teleport back to
    4 landblocks east and a walk west re-bake it inside the radius (its pooled statics must be visible again).
- `tools/rust_parity/gen_world.mjs` writes `crates/holtburger-scene/tests/fixtures/world_<scenario>.json` (2.6 MB total):

## 3. S2: `?rustWorld` shadow mode

### 3.1 The cut: structure mirrored, semantics derived

- **Structure** (complete by construction). `track(bm, kind)` at each draw object's construction inserts a
  per-object prototype (one per original prototype, shared) whose `addGeometry`, `deleteGeometry`, `addInstance`,
  `deleteInstance`, `setMatrixAt`, `setGeometryIdAt`, `setVisibleAt`, `setInstanceCount`, `optimize` and `dispose`
  call three's and then post what happened. Every mutation path is therefore mirrored (the atlas feed alone has six
  unwind paths), and three's own internal calls arrive as three makes them (`deleteGeometry` → `deleteInstance` per
  instance). A prototype, not own properties: film's batch watch tests `hasOwnProperty("setVisibleAt")`.
  The kernel predicts three's id allocation exactly (smallest freed id first, else append; `setInstanceCount`'s
  trailing pop) and counts any id it did not predict.
- **Semantics** (the decisions). One-line hooks post attribution (which landblock / tile / cell owns each instance)
  and the residency / visibility events; the kernel derives each instance's visibility from them with the JS rules
  and NEVER from the raw `setVisibleAt` stream, which it keeps only as a diagnostic mirror (`raw`).
- The audit then compares the derived values with three's `_instanceInfo` and the JS state: a mismatch means a hook
  is missing, a writer the model does not know touched the state, or the kernel's rule is wrong.

### 3.2 The hooks (each `globalThis.__hbRustWorld?.x(...)`: with the flag off the global is undefined and the arguments are not even evaluated)

| File | Hook lines | Event |
|---|---|---|
| `static_batch_x.js` | bucket construction; the feed, after `rec.iids.push` + `setMatrixAt`; `_setLbVisible` | `track chunk`, `ATTR_LB`, `LB_VIS chunk` |
| `static_atlas.js` | bucket construction; the feed's `list.push(row)`; `parkStaticAtlasForLb` / `unparkStaticAtlasForLb` | `track atlas`, `ATTR_LB`, `LB_VIS atlas` |
| `pool_registry.js` | constructor; `poolFor`; `_feedMember` after the born-invisible flip; `commit`; `parkTile`, `adoptTile`, `clearParked`, `releaseTile`, `hideLb`, `showLb`, `cellSetChanged`, `setCellsVisible`, `releaseCells`, `dispose` (method entries) | owner, `track pool`, `POOL_*` |
| `buildings.js` | batch construction | `track building` |
| `landblock_lru.js` | constructor; `track` (both branches); `park`; `_discardStalePoolCopy`; `unpark`; `evict` | owner, `LRU_*` |
| `object_radius.js` | `_hide`, `_show`, the forget loop in `tickObjectRadius` | `OBJR_*` |
| `residency_grid.js` | `SlotGrid` constructor; `setState` after the transition | owner, `TILE_STATE` |
| `cells.js` | `tickCellVisibility3D`, before `lastVisible` rolls forward (the PVS-delta hook only) | `CELL_PVS` |
| `statics.js` | `import "./rust/world.js"` (loads and, with the flag on, arms the bridge at boot) | — |
| `frame_split.js` | `frameSplitCensus().groups` | S0 census |

`pool_producer.js` and `pool_envcells.js` needed no hook: every pool mutation they cause goes through the
registry's methods, and the envcell PVS delta reaches it as `setCellsVisible`.

Membership keys travel exactly as the JS indexes them: the chunk seam masks its argument with `_lbKeyOfId`, the atlas
seam looks up `lbKey >>> 0` unmasked.

### 3.3 The kernel (`crates/holtburger-scene/src/world/`, R2 §2.2)

| Module | Holds |
|---|---|
| `events.rs` | the protocol: opcodes, sections, kinds, tile states, `legal_transition` (residency_grid.js `LEGAL`), field decoding, record lengths |
| `objects.rs` | `DrawObject` (kind, landblock, registry; slots: active, gid, derived `vis`, `raw`, landblock / tile / cell, `committed`, `hidden_cell`, the f32 matrix; free ids; geometry ranges; free gids) |
| `mod.rs` | `World`: objects, the landblock / tile / cell attribution indexes, pool registries (parked tiles, hidden landblocks, per-(tile, pool) `live` records), LRUs (LIVE / PARKED per landblock), grids (tile records with `sinceMs` / `parkedAtMs`), `?objRadius` sets, cell PVS sets, 21 integrity counters, totals, the last audit |
| `apply.rs` | the event rules |
| `audit.rs` | the comparison and the AND-form diagnostic |
| `report.rs` | census (struct + JSON, key for key the model's) and report JSON |
| `tests.rs` | 12 unit tests (their streams were first checked through the JS model; the five added 2026-10-29 also through the compiled SceneWorld where the rule predates them) |

Against R2 §2.2: the **draw object**, **draw item** (per slot: gid, f32 matrix, attribution, visibility),
**visibility** and **LB / tile residency** tables are here. **Geometry refs** are here only structurally (gid →
active, start, count, the free-gid list): the content keys and refcounts stay JS bookkeeping until S6 moves dedup
to Rust. The **placement**, per-band gid, anchor and light tables are not here: their consumers are S3 / S6 / S7.
No three.js math is involved in S2 (nothing is computed from a transform), so `math.rs` is not used.

The JS reference model `tools/rust_parity/gen_world_model.mjs` has the same tables and rules; the Rust is a
port of it, rule for rule, and both are pinned to the same fixtures.

### 3.4 Visibility rules (the exact model)

- **Chunk / atlas**: born visible (three's `addInstance`); a per-landblock seam (`LB_VIS`) writes the value for every
  instance ATTRIBUTED to that landblock in that kind. That is the JS rule exactly (one bit, last writer).
- **Pool**: born invisible and uncommitted; `commit` flips committed instances visible unless the tile is parked or
  the landblock hidden; `parkTile` / `adoptTile` / `hideLb` / `showLb` / `cellSetChanged` / `setCellsVisible`
  re-implemented over the kernel's own membership (committed slots by tile, landblock, cell), the per-(tile, pool)
  `live` flag, the parked-tile set and the hidden-landblock set; `releaseCells` prunes the records it empties.
- **Building**: born visible, never written.
- **The R2 AND form** ("visible = no owner bit set") is computed beside it as a diagnostic, `andDivergence`: chunk /
  atlas `!(LRU parks the landblock || ?objRadius hides it)`; pools `committed && !parked && !landblock hidden && !cell
  hidden`. It was 0 at every checkpoint of every scenario [M node], i.e. on these sequences the JS behaves exactly as
  the AND form S4 would use. One known gap where it would not: a chunk / atlas re-bake of a PARKED landblock paints
  between the feed and the late `track` that re-hides it (an async gap in the live loader; in the scenario both are
  synchronous). The audit would report it as divergence, never as a mismatch.

### 3.5 The audit

- **Arena** (built by the bridge, `WORLD_SEC`): per tracked object its `_instanceInfo` (active, visible, gid); per
  LRU its live and parked landblocks; per grid its records (state, `sinceMs`, `parkedAtMs`); per pool registry its
  parked tiles, hidden landblocks and records (`live`, hidden-cell instance ids); per known scene its `?objRadius` set
  and cell render set; the count of shadow-kind BatchedMeshes in the scene that were never tracked (a missing `track`
  hook); optionally every active instance's matrix and every geometry range.
- **19 categories** (`MISMATCH_KEYS`): unknownObject, missingObject, slotsLen, active, gid, vis, raw, lru, tileState,
  tileTime, objr, cells, poolReg, poolRec, poolHidden, matrix, ranges, untracked, poolHideOrphan (2026-10-29, §11).
  **21 integrity counters** (`INTEGRITY_KEYS`: unpredicted ids, deletes of dead slots, illegal grid transitions, LRU
  desyncs, …). Both must stay 0: `__rustWorld.stats().mismatches` / `.integrity` (and `.poolHideOrphan`, the last
  audit's count of the new category, -1 on a pkg built before it).
- **poolHideOrphan** is not a kernel-vs-JS comparison (like `untracked`, it counts a JS-side fact the arena carries):
  when the arena holds at least one OBJR section, every landblock in a POOLREG section's hidden list that no OBJR
  section of the same arena lists counts 1 (per registry, per landblock). The registry's `_hiddenLbs` is a sticky
  copy of the `?objRadius` hide (`_hide` is `hideLb`'s only product caller), so an entry objRadius no longer holds is
  a drifted owner bit. No OBJR section (`?objRadius` off or not yet ticked, or a registry driven alone as in the
  `pool` scenario): nothing to compare with, 0.
- Owners (LRU, grid, registry) register at construction, so a missing event hook shows up as a mismatch instead of
  an owner nobody audits. A disposed object (three nulls `_matricesTexture`) that was never reported is left out of
  the arena, so the kernel reports it missing; it is never healed. A garbage-collected one is dropped (WeakRef).
- **Periodic** (1 Hz, browser): the residency sections every time, the instance tables of a rotating window of at
  most 4,096 slots (the rest listed deferred), matrices and ranges every 10th audit. `__rustWorld.audit()`
  compares everything.
- **Film**: a take holding a batch hide shadows the mesh's `setVisibleAt` with an own property; such objects are
  skipped (counted `filmHeld`), because film's restore rule ("only if no foreign write since") is not a residency
  fact. After the take they are compared again.

### 3.6 Costs [M node 20 on the laptop, best of 5; noisy]

- Flag off: one global property load per event at the hook sites (feeds, parks, transitions) and one per frame
  in cells.js; the optional call short-circuits before evaluating its arguments.
- Flag on, per mutation: 20,000 `addInstance` + `setMatrixAt` + attribution 53 → 117 ms (about +3.2 µs each, the
  matrix copy and the queue); 20,000 `setVisibleAt` 0.8 → 7.9 ms (+0.35 µs each).
- Flag on, audit: a full audit of one 20,000-instance object on the JS model kernel 21 ms (142 ms with matrices);
  hence the 4,096-slot window for the periodic audit. At 20,000 slots over 400 objects the bridge's arena build for
  a windowed audit is 1.3 ms [M]; the JS model's comparison adds 5–8 ms (it also runs the AND diagnostic over every
  slot), which is the part the compiled kernel replaces — its timing is owed (W section, then a boot).
- Scenario wall time armed vs disarmed: chunk 17 → 32 ms, grid 53 → 48 ms (noise dominates).

## 4. Invariants kept (R2 §3)

| R2 # | How |
|---|---|
| 1 dispose ownership | the kernel names nothing; it never disposes or mutates a JS object |
| 2 entries XOR parkPool | one LB state per LRU; JS dual state shows as an `lru` mismatch; `LRU_DROP_POOL` for the non-destructive recovery |
| 5 LIVE flip last | pool members are born invisible and uncommitted until `commit` |
| 6 sticky `?objRadius` | pools: the registry's sticky set, re-implemented; chunk / atlas: the seams the JS calls, mirrored. 2026-10-29: the registry copy is cross-checked against objRadius's own (`poolHideOrphan`), and objRadius's forget now lifts it (§11) |
| 9 integrity counters | grid `LEGAL` table checked on every transition, `tileDesync`, LRU desyncs; all asserted 0 |
| 14 film hides | film-held objects skipped, never modelled |
| 21 `setGeometryIdAt` raises nothing | mirrored structurally (`INST_GID`), visibility unaffected |
| 29 raycast / film read three's flags | untouched: three's state is never written |
| 31 exact matrices | the f32 values three stored are mirrored and compared bit for bit |
| 35 `?nullRender` / `?renderOnDemand` | no frame dependency: events and a timer |
| 37 context loss | nothing GPU-side |

## 5. Verification

Run here (node 20, laptop, one at a time, each after checking the build cgroup is empty and ≥ 1.5 GB available):

- `node tests/rust_world_shadow.test.mjs`: **103/103** with the JS model kernel; the W section SKIPs ("pkg/ has no
  SceneWorld"). M1 every checkpoint of 6 scenarios 0 / 0; M2 armed == disarmed JS state at every checkpoint; M3
  one-batch replay == live, 11 perturbations caught in exactly the right categories, malformed arenas / batches
  refused; M4 **35 knock-out mutants** (every semantic hook the scenarios reach, every structural wrapper but
  `_onCount`, which M5 checks directly with `cellPvs`) each make the shadow fail; M5 foreign writes, film, cell PVS, `setInstanceCount`, untracked
  objects, the audit window; M6 flag grammar, the pkg lookup (class present → used; class missing or another `abi()` → disarmed, warned once; events posted before the pkg boots are buffered, then applied in order; the 1 Hz timer audits on its own and stops on disarm), the S0 census.
- `node tools/rust_parity/gen_world.mjs`: 6 fixtures, all clean, deterministic.
- **97 existing suites** (every `tests/*.mjs`, `harness/test_*.mjs`, `test_*.mjs` that loads a hooked file), each run
  flag off and with `node --import ./tools/rust_parity/gen_world_arm.mjs` (hooks armed on the JS model), twice
  (the second run on the final code): **same stdout and exit code** once timing numbers are normalized (13 suites
  print timings), except two that are nondeterministic on their own: `test_frame_split_probe.mjs` asserts measured
  ms against synthetic spin costs and failed once in each arm over 3 + 3 repeats (passing in the others), and
  `tests/structure_p0_probe.test.mjs` polls a wall-clock settle (two flag-off runs differ in 19 normalized lines).
  Neither has a tracked object or a hook event in the measured code. The arm's exit audit
  (stderr) reads 0 mismatches / 0 integrity in 95; the other two (`test_landblock_lru_frame_slot.mjs`,
  `test_landblock_lru_pool_scan.mjs`) write the LRU's maps directly (a `_reclaim` stub, a `parkPool` spy), which the
  shadow correctly reports.
- That run caught one regression of mine: `test_stat_geom_dedup.mjs` check 37 is a source-text regex requiring the
  feed's `if (rec) rec.iids.push(iid);` to be followed directly by `bm.setMatrixAt`, and the attribution hook sat
  between them (failing in both arms). The hook now follows `setMatrixAt` (which cannot throw for an id
  `addInstance` just returned, so the attributed set is the same); the suite is 40/40 in both arms and the
  fixtures were regenerated.

- An independent read-only review of the Rust against the model (a careful read for rustc 1.95 / edition 2024, not
  a build) found no compile errors and no divergence in counters, visibility, record lengths or census JSON; two
  diagnostic sample strings were aligned with the model's afterwards. One model-only limit it noted: the JS
  model's slot key `h × 2^32 + iid` loses precision past 2^21 handles (the Rust uses tuples).

Owed to the orchestrator:

- `cargo test -p holtburger-scene` (new: `world::events::tests` 3, `world::objects::tests` 2, `world::tests` 7,
  `tests/world_parity.rs` 4).
- wasm: then `HB_PKG=pkg-rustcore node tests/rust_world_shadow.test.mjs` — its W section must PASS (every scenario 0 / 0
  through the compiled kernel, the compiled census string equal to the model's at every checkpoint, the 6 fixtures
  replayed), not SKIP.
- One SwiftShader boot with `?rustWorld=on`: `__rustWorld.audit()` and `.stats()` must read 0 mismatches and 0
  integrity after streaming settles and after an `@teleloc` hop (R2 §4 S2 proof).

## 6. Findings

1. **The atlas empty-bucket GC never disposes the BatchedMesh** [C `static_atlas.js` `tickStatAtlasOptimize`, the
   `texCompressedOnlyActive()` loop]: it removes the bucket and disposes its arrays, material and geometry, but not
   `bm` itself, so each GC'd (preview-dim) bucket leaks its matrices and indirect DataTextures (GPU textures once
   drawn). One-line fix, not applied (a behaviour change): `try { b.bm.dispose(); } catch (_) {}` after the geometry
   dispose. The shadow copes (the handle drops when the WeakRef dies).
2. On every scripted sequence, the chunk / atlas / pool visibility the JS produces equals R2's AND form (§3.4), so
   S4's bit model holds there; the async re-bake-while-parked gap is the one known exception. **Corrected
   2026-10-29**: for pools the AND form reads the registry's OWN copy of the `?objRadius` bit (`_hiddenLbs`), so it
   cannot see that copy drift from objRadius's set — which the product did (§11: the forget left the registry's hide
   behind; AND-form divergence read 0 on the drifted run too). The `poolHideOrphan` category now ties the two copies.
3. R2 §1.6-style premise checks: pools are AND-consistent by the registry's own logic (commit, adopt, show and the
   cell flips all test the same three facts) — given the registry's hidden set is objRadius's (now audited, §11); the
   chunk and atlas seams are single-bit last-writer, made consistent by the callers' guards (`_show` skips the unpark
   of a parked landblock, `afterUnpark` re-hides).

## 7. Not done, and why

- **S4 `?rustWorldLists` (opaque chunk buckets): not built.** The precondition was "S2 done and proven"; S2 is not
  proven until the kernel compiles and the W section and a boot read 0. Two further reasons to measure before
  building it:
  - Under `?staticEarlyOut` (default on since 10-23) the unsorted chunk buckets already skip three's rebuild on every
    settled frame, so S4 saves the rebuild only on frames whose visibility changed. R2's −0.15 to −0.3 ms came from
    the 10-23 profiles; re-measure the change-frame cost on the 1070 first.
  - Its value is mostly as the input to R3's draw list.

  What S4 needs from lane X2 (`batched_runs.js`):
  - Nothing to start: the S4 adapter is a new list writer, and it joins through the existing
    `markBatchedRunsOwnHook(mesh)` + `reportBatchedRunsList(mesh, wrote)` contract (writer list, header §L1), so
    `_prepare` compares or skips exactly as for the memo overrides.
  - Optional, to skip `buildRuns` on change frames: `setBatchedRunsExternal(mesh, runs)` with
    `runs = { epoch, n, r, starts: Int32Array(r), counts: Int32Array(r), inst: Int32Array(r), layout: Uint32Array(1 + r + n) }`
    built by Rust with `buildRuns`' exact semantics (runs in first-seen order, ids in canonical order within a run,
    `layout = [0xFFFFFFFF, runStart_0..r-1, ids…]`, `-1` on a start seen with two counts). `_prepare` would use it
    as the run state when `runs.epoch` equals the mesh's L1 epoch and the canonical arrays are the ones stamped,
    else fall back to its own build.
  What S4 itself needs, on top of today's tables (which already hold, per opaque chunk bucket, slot → active, gid,
  derived visibility, and gid → start / count from `GEOM_ADD` / `GEOM_RANGES`):
  - kernel `lists.rs`: a per-object list epoch bumped by any active / gid / visibility change; the active list
    (visible ∧ active, ascending slot order = three's unsorted rebuild); multidraw starts = `start ×
    bytesPerElement × multiplier`, counts = `count × multiplier` (both supplied by JS per object); the run layout
    with `buildRuns` semantics; one `frame()` call returning the dirty objects' lists in one arena;
  - JS adapter: for each dirty object write `_multiDrawStarts` / `_multiDrawCounts` / `_multiDrawCount` /
    `_indirectTexture.image.data` (+ `needsUpdate`), leave `_visibilityChanged` false, `reportBatchedRunsList`; a boot
    self-test that disarms loudly on three drift (R2 §5 risk 2);
  - parity: lists and layouts bit-equal to three's own `onBeforeRender` + `buildRuns` over the fixtures' states.
- **S3** (`?rustWorldVis`) needs the node-route records (placements, spheres, the cull exemptions) and lane C's
  kernel applied to them; S2's cell render set and objRadius / LRU tables are its inputs.
- **S5 / S6 / S7**: out of today's scope (R2 ordering: S2, then one population flipped at a time).
- **Node routes** (singletons, LODs, cell containers) are not in the instance audit; their visibility is lane C's
  walk. The cell render set is mirrored (for S3).
- **Film** is skipped, not modelled (§3.5).
- **Per-LB `?staticBatch` batches** (statics.js `consolidateStaticSingletons`) and the terrain batch are not tracked:
  the per-LB batches only appear when the chunk batcher consumed nothing; the terrain batch is out of stage 2. The
  census counts both.

The static world's draw objects (chunk / atlas buckets, pools, building batches), instance attribution and residency (LRU, slot grid, pool registry, `?objRadius`, cell PVS) mirrored in Rust (`SceneWorld`), which derives every instance's visibility from the residency events; a 1 Hz audit compares with three's `_instanceInfo` and the JS state. ## 9. Risks: check these first

1. **The Rust is uncompiled.** It is a port of `gen_world_model.mjs`; the most likely failures are borrow-checker
   complaints in `apply.rs` (pool arms hold `self.regs`, `self.idx` and `self.objects` at once, all disjoint fields)
   and `audit.rs`. The fixtures pin behaviour, so a compile fix must not change a rule.
2. **A writer the model does not know.** A future setVisibleAt caller, or a new per-landblock seam, shows as `vis`
   mismatches with `raw` agreeing. That is the shadow doing its job; extend the model and the Rust together.
3. **The prototype insertion** changes `Object.getPrototypeOf(bm)` of tracked objects (flag on only). Nothing in
   scene3d compares prototypes [C grep]; instance checks and `constructor` are unchanged.
4. **Shadow-mode cost** (flag on): ~3 µs per instance add at bake time, one bounded audit per second. Fine for a
   diagnostic arm; not for an A/B of frame time.
5. **Two ids from one owner** cannot happen in the browser (one LRU, one grid, one registry); the kernel keys every
   table by owner id anyway, so tests with several stay separate.

## 11. 2026-10-29: review r2 fixes (lane W)

The adversarial review of round 2 (`review_r2.json`, lane W) confirmed four findings; all four are fixed here.
Evidence tags as above; every run below is node on the laptop, one at a time, ≥ 2 GB available, no cargo / wasm /
browser.

### 11.1 `?objRadius` forget left the pool registry's sticky hide behind (DEFAULT-ON, wrong pixels; pre-existing)

- **Bug** [C]: `tickObjectRadius`'s forget loop dropped an evicted landblock from `st.hidden` only. The registry's
  `_hiddenLbs` (its sticky copy of the hide) loses an entry only in `showLb`, reached only from `_show`, which needs
  `st.hidden.has(k)`. So: hide (d > N + 1) → tile parked and released (grid pressure pass / teleport; baked marks
  deleted) → next crossing forgets → the player comes back, the tile re-feeds and `commit()` skips every member
  (`_lbHides`): the landblock's pooled statics stay invisible until objRadius happens to hide and show it again.
- **Fix** (`scene3d/object_radius.js` `_forget`): the forget also calls `scene3d._poolShowLb(k)`, fail-soft, after
  clearing `st.hidden` (same order as before for objRadius's own set); `forgets` stat added (`__objRadius()`).
  Safe on the grid path: a landblock leaves the baked sets only through a grid release of a PARKED tile, so `showLb`
  finds the tile parked (`live` false) or released and flips nothing; it only drops the mark (pinned: objRadius
  suite 6c). Chain off: `_poolShowLb` is index.js's wrapper returning 0 without a registry (and a scene without the
  hook is a no-op, 6h). `?objRadius=off`: `tickObjectRadius` returns first, unchanged. `?rustWorld`: `showLb` posts
  POOL_SHOW_LB, so the kernel follows with no Rust change.
- **Other un-mark paths** [C]: `statics.js` un-marks `staticsBakedLbs` only for a bake in flight (fetch failure /
  starvation retry, sealed abort) — before `afterObjectBake`, so never for a landblock objRadius already hides (a
  hidden landblock is baked, and the loaders short-circuit a baked one); `landblock_lru.js` `_discardStalePoolCopy`
  drops only the `buildingsBakedLbs` mark, and only when the landblock has no live building node. So the forget
  fires on eviction (grid release / LRU evict) in practice. Should a hidden landblock ever lose both marks while its
  pooled members were LIVE, they would now show until its next bake's `afterObjectBake` re-hides them (before: hidden
  for the session).
- **Regression checks**: `test_object_radius.mjs` 5f / 5g (fake registry: the forget issues exactly one `poolShow`
  for the evicted landblock, nothing else) and section 6 (the REAL `PoolRegistry`, wired as index.js wires it: hide →
  park → forget flips nothing but drops the mark → release → back → re-baked visible; release-before-forget; fail-soft
  / chain-off); `tests/rust_world_shadow.test.mjs` M7 + M1 / M3 over the new `objrPool` scenario (the grid path:
  A and A2's pooled statics `[1,1]` after the walk back). Against the HEAD `object_radius.js` (scratch copies, the
  tree untouched): objRadius suite 40 passed / 5 failed (5f, 6c, 6d, 6f, 6g; 45/45 fixed); shadow suite 150 / 5
  failed (M1 objrPool, M3 objrPool replay, three M7 checks; 155/155 fixed).

### 11.2 The audit could not see that drift (the cross-check)

- The kernel mirrors objr's set and the registry's `hidden_lbs` faithfully but never compared them, and the pool
  branch of the AND form reads the registry copy: the drifted run read 0 mismatches, 0 integrity, 0 andDivergence.
- **New category `poolHideOrphan`** (model `gen_world_model.mjs` audit, Rust `audit.rs` / `mod.rs`: `MISMATCH_KEYS`
  19, `mk::POOL_HIDE_ORPHAN = 18`, `LastAudit.cat: [u64; 19]`); the exact rule is in §3.5. The fixed product reads 0
  at every checkpoint of every scenario; the pre-fix forget replayed (`objrPool` with `opts.preFixForget`, which
  drops the forget's show only — `_show`'s passes) reads 0 0 0 0 18 12 12 12 over the checkpoints, the only category
  counted, and leaves A / A2 at `[0,0]` after the walk back. Bridge: `stats().poolHideOrphan` (the last audit's count;
  −1 when the kernel's report lacks the key, i.e. a stale pkg). `WORLD_ABI` unchanged (no event or arena layout
  changed).
- The AND form is unchanged (a diagnostic; with poolHideOrphan 0 the registry copy equals objRadius's on every
  landblock the registry hides).
- **Fixtures**: `objrPool` added to `gen_world_scenarios.mjs` (the grid world factored into `gridWorld()`; the `grid`
  scenario's calls are the same in the same order) and to `world_parity.rs` `SCENARIOS`; a generator recipe renames a
  pool-hidden landblock (`poolReg` 2 + `poolHideOrphan` 1). Regenerated: the six old fixtures differ from their
  10-26 versions ONLY in `mismatch_keys` (events, arenas, censuses, negatives identical); `world_objrPool.json` is 8
  checkpoints (all 0), 36 negatives, 4 of them orphans; two runs md5-identical. Total 2.9 MB.
- **Regression checks**: node M7 (fixed run 0 everywhere and stat 0; the pool scenario's registry-only hides not
  cross-checked; the pre-fix replay counted and in `stats()`); M3 perturbation `{poolReg: 2, poolHideOrphan: 1}`;
  cargo `world::tests::pool_hide_orphans_are_cross_checked_against_the_objr_sets` (forget → 1, show → 0, section
  order free, union of scenes, no OBJR section → 0, one count per registry) and
  `world_parity::the_pool_hide_cross_check_is_pinned` (the objrPool fixture carries OBJR_FORGET, POOL_HIDE_LB,
  POOL_SHOW_LB and orphan negatives, which `negatives_are_caught_category_for_category` checks category for
  category). Against the HEAD model: shadow suite 150 / 5 failed (four M7 checks, the M3 perturbation). The
  compiled pkg/ (built before this) fails the 4 orphan asserts of the Rust test's stream (mirror script) — i.e. the
  new cargo test fails on the pre-fix Rust.
